regions.name: Western Pacific warm pool
regions.why: The tropical atmosphere above the warmest ocean on Earth, from the surface to the tropopause.

regions.name: Indo-Gangetic Plain (Delhi)
regions.why: One of the most populated, polluted and irrigated plains on Earth.

T2M.label: Air temperature
T2M.simple: How warm the air is 2 metres above the ground — what a thermometer in the shade shows.

PRECTOTCORR.label: Precipitation
PRECTOTCORR.simple: How much rain and snow falls, in millimetres of water per day (1 mm on one square metre is one litre). MERRA-2 corrects its model rain with rain gauges and satellite observations.

TQV.label: Water vapour in the air column
TQV.simple: All the water vapour above a spot, from the ground to the top of the atmosphere — the millimetres of water you would get if it all rained out at once.

SLP.label: Sea-level pressure
SLP.simple: The weight of the air above a spot, as if measured at sea level (about 1013 hPa on average): low pressure brings storms, high pressure fair weather.

story.text: One process in Western Pacific warm pool and Indo-Gangetic Plain (Delhi): in each, precipitation and water vapour in the air column leave their norm in the same months the same way — the same transformation carries one onto the other in every region.

Air temperature — Western Pacific warm pool: +0.21 °C per decade (95 % range +0.176 to +0.241). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 4e-16, t-test p = 4.1e-12. Eva: Since 2011, 80 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Precipitation — Indo-Gangetic Plain (Delhi): +0.18 mm/day per decade (95 % range +0.104 to +0.258). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 1.6e-05, t-test p = 0.00095. Eva: Since 2011, 67 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Water vapour in the air column — Indo-Gangetic Plain (Delhi): +1.1 kg/m² per decade (95 % range +0.707 to +1.44). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 3.6e-06, t-test p = 1.4e-06. Eva: Since 2011, 71 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Precipitation (Western Pacific warm pool) and Water vapour in the air column (Western Pacific warm pool) leave their norm in the same months, the same way: 51 times, where chance at the same moment of the record would give 16 (p = 2e-15; z = 11.6 against the same reading with one of them moved 1 to 5 years, beyond the shared trend and the persistence of each). Model note: both series come from the MERRA-2 reanalysis, not from two independent instruments: confirm it with an independent dataset before calling it a finding.
